title: Minimize the Difference Between Target and Chosen Elements
summary: Given an m x n integer matrix and a target, select one element from each row to minimize the absolute difference between the target and the sum of the selected elements.
statement: Given an m x n integer matrix and a target, select one element from each row to minimize the absolute difference between the target and the sum of the selected elements. Return this minimum difference.
constraints: mat has 1 through 70 rows and columns, with positive values at most 70.
Choose exactly one number from each row.
Return the minimum absolute difference between the chosen sum and target.
hints: After each row, only the set of reachable partial sums matters.
Start with sum zero and combine every reachable sum with every value in the next row.
possible={0}; for row: possible={s+x for s in possible for x in row}; minimize distance to target.
Induction shows the set contains exactly all sums formed by one choice from every processed row, so the final minimum checks every legal selection.
editorial: Induction shows the set contains exactly all sums formed by one choice from every processed row, so the final minimum checks every legal selection.

tests.explanation: Choosing one, five, and seven reaches thirteen exactly, so the difference is zero.
The only possible sum is six, which is ninety-four away from the target.
